name: Central bank stress
value: Dec Fed rise priced ~98%; yen near 160/$
summary: Fed minutes show almost all officials favour more rises; markets price a December move as Japan warns on the yen
state: Minutes of the Fed's October meeting, released on 18 Nov, showed almost all officials judged further rate rises likely appropriate, and CME FedWatch put the chance of a December rise at about 98% (XTB; New Straits Times). Gold fell to its lowest since September 2025 on 18 Nov on the hawkish signals. Japan's currency official Mimura warned on 12 Nov that yen moves were too rapid as the dollar neared 160 yen, but no new intervention was found as of 20 Nov.
for_you: Borrowing costs in the US are expected to rise further, and markets are volatile. The Bank of England publishes its own rate decisions and explanations for UK households.
rubric_hit: Stagflationary dilemma and Japanese warnings on yen near 160 meet Watch; no emergency move or coordinated intervention

sources.title: XTB — Fed minutes: virtually everyone in favour of further rate hikes
New Straits Times — Gold drops 2pct to over one-year low as hawkish Fed signals boost dollar
New Straits Times — Japan's Mimura says markets shouldn't forget intervention risks as yen nears 160

why: Central banks are the shock absorbers; when they are boxed in or their independence is challenged, markets lose their backstop.
drivers: Inflation vs growth trade-off, political pressure, currency moves, financial stability.

rubric.alert: Emergency inter-meeting moves, attempt to remove a central-bank head, or coordinated intervention.
rubric.watch: Stagflationary dilemma, open political pressure on a major central bank, or FX intervention by a G7 bank.
rubric.normal: Fed, ECB and BoJ acting orderly and on schedule; independence unquestioned.
